title: A Phase 3 Efficacy and Safety Study of HBS-301 in Participants with Narcolepsy
official: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-Controlled, Efficacy and Safety Study of HBS-301 in Participants with Narcolepsy Followed by an Open-label Extension
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of HBS-301 compared with placebo in treating  excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS)
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Is able to provide voluntary, written informed consent.
2. 2. Has a current documented diagnosis of NT1 or NT2 per ICSD-3 or ICSD-3-TR criteria with either a confirmatory diagnostic hypocretin level (ICSD-3-TR) or PSG with MSLT report on file completed within the last 10 years.
3. 3. Is male or female, ≥18 years at the time of Screening.
4. 4. CCI.
5. 5. CCI.
6. 6. If taking a permitted chronic concomitant medication or supplement, including nonprohibited antidepressants or wake-promoting agents, must be on a stable dose for at least 3 months prior to Screening and agree to continue at that stable dose for the Double-blind Treatment Period of the study. Pro re nata (PRN ) use of any treatment that could affect daytime sleepiness (including but not limited to oxybates, stimulants, modafinil, and armodafinil) is not permitted.
7. 7. For participants being treated for OSA or other hypoventilatory conditions, participants must be compliant with their medical device or oral appliance as determined by the Investigator. Participants must maintain OSA treatment compliance throughout the study.
8. 8. A participant who is a female of childbearing potential (FCBP) must have a negative serum pregnancy test at Screening, a negative urine pregnancy test at Baseline and agree to remain abstinent or use a highly effective method of nonhormonal contraception to prevent pregnancy while receiving study drug and for 30 days after the final dose of study drug. Participants who are FCBPs using hormonal contraception must also use a highly effective nonhormonal contraceptive method while receiving study drug and for at least 30 days after the final dose of study drug. An FCBP is defined as a female who is postmenarcheal, has an intact uterus and at least 1 ovary, and is <1 year postmenopausal. Male participants who are not azoospermic (vasectomized or sterile due to a medical cause) must agree to remain abstinent or use an effective method of contraception while receiving study drug and for 30 days after the final dose of study drug.
9. 9. In the opinion of the Investigator, participant is capable of understanding and complying with the requirements of the protocol and administration of oral study drug.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Has hypersomnia due to another medical disorder.
2. 10. Has a known history of long QT syndrome or any significant history of a serious abnormality of the ECG (e.g., recent [at least 1 year] myocardial infarction, clinically significant arrhythmia).
3. 11. Has a family history of sudden cardiac death, unexplained death, or death from a primary dysrhythmia potentially associated with QT prolongation in any family member.
4. 12. Has a QTcF with a mean value of >450 msec (QTcF=QT/3√ RR) at Screening or Baseline based on the mean of triplicate 12-lead ECGs.
5. 13. Has a current or recent (within 1 year) history of a substance use disorder or dependence disorder, including alcohol and caffeine use disorders as defined in the DSM-V.
6. 14. Has surgery planned during the Screening/Baseline or Double-blind Treatment Periods.
7. 15. Has received a prohibited medication within 5 half-lives of the medication prior to Screening. Prohibited medications include strong CYP3A4 inducers, centrally acting H1R antagonists, non-benzodiazepine hypnotics, and medications that prolong the QT interval.
8. 16. Has received a medication PRN that could affect daytime sleepiness (including but not limited to oxybates, stimulants, modafinil, and armodafinil) within 5 half-lives of the medication prior to Screening.
9. 17. Has a positive urine drug screen except for medications that are prescribed by an HCP or under the supervision of an HCP for medical conditions and are not otherwise prohibited in the study.
10. 18. Has a significant risk of committing suicide based on history, routine psychiatric examination, Investigator’s judgment, or answering “yes” to Question 4 or 5 on the C-SSRS at Screening or Baseline, or with any suicidal behavior in the last 12 months before Screening.
11. 19. Has a history of seizures.
12. 2. Has a history of pitolisant use within 5 half-lives prior to Screening.
13. 20. Is currently breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed over the course of the study. Lactating women must agree not to breastfeed for the duration of the study and for 7 days after their final dose of study drug.
14. 21. Based on the judgment of the Investigator, is unsuitable for the study for any reason, including but not limited to unstable or uncontrolled medical conditions (including psychiatric, neurological, or gastrointestinal conditions or procedures [e.g., bariatric surgery or weight loss surgery that may affect study drug absorption]), or a medical condition that might interfere with the conduct of the study, confound interpretation of study results, pose a health risk to the participant, or compromise the integrity of the study.
15. 22. If required by local regulations, participant must be insured by appropriate national health insurance system.
16. 3. Participated in an interventional research study involving another investigational medication, device, or behavioral treatment within 30 days or within 5 half-lives of the investigational medication prior to Screening (whichever is longer).
17. 4. Has a primary diagnosis of psychiatric illness, including depression, that is not well controlled (i.e., symptoms and medications have not been stable for at least 3 months prior to Screening).
18. 5. Has any history of bipolar disorder or psychosis.
19. 6. Has acute or chronic liver disease or a history of moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class B) or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C).
20. 7. Has a BSA-corrected eGFR <60 mL/min at Screening as calculated by the central laboratory.
21. 8. Has 1 or more abnormal Screening laboratory values that are clinically significant as determined by the Investigator.
22. 9. Has a medical history known to increase risk for proarrhythmia (e.g., recent [at least 1 year] myocardial infarction, heart failure, bradyarrhythmias, tachyarrhythmias, ventricular arrhythmias, torsade de pointes, unstable angina, high-degree atrioventricular block).
